solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prepare to beat up silly person

parts.note: to do food is to prepare it
slang: to do someone over is to beat them up

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready to thrash a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The same two-letter verb serves twice, once in its kitchen sense and once in its thuggish one.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct flightless bird gave its name to a dull-witted, foolish person, as in 'you dodo!'

clue.text: Conductor is likely to make this movement relaxed

definitions.text: Conductor is likely to make this movement
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the downward stroke of a baton marking the first beat of a bar

explanation.walkthrough: Movement looks musical in the sense of a section of a symphony, but it is the conductor's gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: The conductor's accented first beat is shown by a downward motion of the hand, and the same word describes a calm, understated mood.

clue.text: Almost bashful objection

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: demure means modest and shy

explanation.surface: A shy, half-hearted protest.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a demur is an expression of hesitation or a protest, as in 'without demur'.

clue.text: Reserve best spades — mountaineers might need them

parts.note: ice is cool reserve or formality of manner
the pick of the bunch is the best
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Keep your finest spades in reserve, as climbers may need them.
explanation.walkthrough: Spades and climbing suggest digging tools, but spades only supplies a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers on glaciers and frozen faces use small axes with pointed heads to chip footholds, so mountaineers might need them.

clue.text: Chief of Staff to dismiss cavalryman

indicators.note: to here means added to, so one piece is placed next to the other

parts.note: COS is the standard abbreviation for Chief of Staff
to sack is to fire from a job

explanation.surface: A senior officer is told to discharge a mounted soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossacks were famed horsemen of the Russian and Ukrainian steppes who served as light cavalry.

clue.text: Newspaper editor on tour — something that makes an impression on the board

definitions.text: something that makes an impression on the board

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the earlier pieces sit over the later one

parts.note: print is the press, the newspaper world
ED is the abbreviation for editor
a circuit is a round tour, as of judges or performers

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor travelling makes an impact on the company board.
explanation.walkthrough: The board in the definition is an electronic circuit board, not a board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Its conducting tracks are printed or etched onto an insulating board, so it literally leaves its mark on that board.

clue.text: Try to pull cart up enclosed area

parts.note: to court someone is to try to win their affections

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dray is a low, heavy cart

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a cart uphill into a walled space.
explanation.walkthrough: Pull is British slang for attracting a romantic partner, so 'try to pull' means woo.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtyard is an open space surrounded by walls or buildings, so it is an enclosed area.

clue.text: Use needle and thread to cover the small hole

indicators.note: to cover means to wrap around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: sewing is working with needle and thread
a shortened form of the, as in the dialect t'

explanation.surface: Instructions to darn over a little hole.
explanation.walkthrough: Hole is not a tear in cloth but a predicament: being in a hole means being in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a stew means being in a state of anxiety or trouble, just as being in a hole is a difficult situation.

clue.text: Man of the match's gift?

parts.note: surface reading: the award to the best player in a sporting fixture; setter's reading: the match is a marriage, and the man in it gives his fiancée a token on becoming betrothed

explanation.walkthrough: Man of the match sounds like a football award, but the match is a romantic pairing and the gift is the token of a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: A man proposing marriage traditionally gives his intended a ring to mark their betrothal.

clue.text: Game's tense after animosity

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the next one

parts.note: pique is resentment or ill feeling
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A match grows strained after bad feeling between players.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquet is a centuries-old two-player card game played with a 32-card pack.

clue.text: Group of females two men insist gets changed in front of truck

indicators.note: in front of tells us the reworked letters come first and the next piece follows them
something that gets changed is altered in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
a ute is a utility vehicle, a small pickup truck in Australian usage

explanation.surface: A gang of women hears two men demand a change before a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: UTE, short for utility vehicle, is common in Australia and New Zealand for a pickup.
explanation.definitionFit: The Women's Institute is a British organisation for women, famous for its jam-making and community meetings, so it is a group of females.

clue.text: Cuban radar at sea missing navy's fearsome swimmer

indicators.note: at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters are jumbled
missing says the following item is absent from the letters

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
N is a standard abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: Cuban naval radar out at sea picks up a frightening creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the N from the ten letters, then rearrange the remaining nine.
explanation.definitionFit: This large predatory fish has sharp teeth and a reputation for ferocity, so it is a fearsome creature of the water.

clue.text: Carry child 1back to house

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only the end is kept

parts.note: the final letter of house

explanation.surface: Lug the youngster home to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray '1' before 'back' is a typesetting slip in the source and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is an informal verb meaning to carry, especially something heavy or a weapon.

clue.text: Doctor late in catching male's illness

indicators.note: catching means holding onto something, so one piece goes inside the other
to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A doctor turns up late to diagnose a man's sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a noun for the physician in the scene but is a verb telling us to alter the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is a minor sickness or disorder, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Fight rugby player — cut head to toe

parts.note: a lock is a second-row forward in rugby

indicators.note: head to toe says the first letter is moved to the end of the word

parts.note: shorn means cut, as of hair or fleece

explanation.surface: A rugby forward is gashed from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Stags literally entangle antlers when they clash, so the idiom means to engage in conflict or argue.

clue.text: Take issue

parts.note: surface reading: to disagree or object to something; setter's reading: issue means offspring, so this is to take someone's child away by force

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for arguing hides a literal reading: issue is a legal word for children, and taking a child unlawfully is abduction.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct someone, originally a child, and hold them is the crime named by the answer.

clue.text: Run then collapse? Sign of distress

indicators.note: then says one piece follows directly after the other

parts.note: to tear along is to run fast
to drop is to fall down exhausted

explanation.surface: Someone sprints until they keel over, a worrying symptom.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop shed from the eye shows sorrow or upset, so it signals distress.

clue.text: Head of ENT came prepared to contain unknown skin disease

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of ENT

indicators.note: to contain means to hold within, so one piece sits inside the other
something prepared has been worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: The ear, nose and throat consultant arrived ready to deal with a mysterious rash.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT is the hospital department for ear, nose and throat; here it only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eczema is an inflammatory condition causing itchy, dry, red patches, so it is a dermatological complaint.

clue.text: Someone desperate to enter stake — but not quickly

indicators.note: to enter means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake put in before the deal
Desperate Dan is the cowboy hero of the British children's comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A frantic gambler rushes to bet, though not in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan, the giant cow-pie-eating strongman, is a British comic-strip character, so 'someone desperate' points to his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical direction for a moderate, walking pace, slower than allegro.

clue.text: Flag raised; wind lessened to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent means only partly, so the answer is a portion of the words before

parts.note: the letters run across the end of raised, all of wind and the start of lessened

explanation.surface: A flag is hoisted, and the breeze drops a little.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag looks like a noun for a banner being raised, but it is the verb meaning to weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or diminish, and to dwindle is to grow gradually smaller, so both verbs mean decline.

clue.text: Lying tethered up outside church

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
outside says one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: tied means tethered
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone lies bound outside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Lying looks like a position, as in lying tethered, but it is the noun meaning telling untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in the sense of dishonest behaviour is a synonym of deceit, the practice of misleading people.

clue.text: Chap eating hot rabbit

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: slang: a cat is a man or fellow, as in a cool cat
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A man tucking into spicy rabbit stew.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit is not an animal here: in British slang (from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk) to rabbit is to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses rabbit as a verb meaning to talk at length, a close synonym of the informal word for conversation.

clue.text: Daughter: check around and look for a place to sit

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: around suggests moving things about, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
an air is a look or appearance, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: A parent tells their daughter to scout about for a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding canvas seat used on beaches and ship decks is literally somewhere to sit.

clue.text: Part female rejected? He might not

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a woman turned down in part, or a part of something female thrown out
setter's reading: a male performer might refuse a female role, though in pantomime he might take it

explanation.walkthrough: Part means a role in a play: a man who performs might decline a woman's role, or might play it, as dames do in British pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who plays parts on stage or screen is a male performer, the person who might reject a female role.

clue.text: A passenger leaving employee's tip at a distance

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the word

parts.note: a fare is a paying passenger in a taxi

indicators.note: a tip is an end point, here the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of employee

explanation.surface: A taxi passenger leaves without tipping the driver, from a distance.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip suggests money for the driver, but it is the end of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is an adverb meaning far away or from a long way off.

clue.text: Straw was damaged in strong fire — I'm storing last of rye

definitions.note: a phrase completing 'Straw was a ...' rather than a bare noun

indicators.note: storing means keeping something inside, so one piece is held within the other
damaged means broken up, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of rye

explanation.surface: A straw harvest was ruined in a fierce blaze, with rye stored somewhere in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Straw is Jack Straw, the British Labour politician who served as Foreign Secretary from 2001 to 2006; the farm picture of straw and rye is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Straw held Britain's top diplomatic post, the cabinet office known elsewhere by the generic title of the answer.

clue.text: Engaged again; calmly submissive

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., taken on under a new contract
second meaning: accepting something unwelcome without protest

explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-SIGNED, the word describes a player or employee given a fresh contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has accepted their fate without fighting it is described with the same spelling as a person who signed up a second time.

clue.text: Tiger's first hit bunker

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of Tiger
a rap is a sharp knock or blow

explanation.surface: Tiger Woods's opening shot lands in a bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: The golfer Tiger Woods sets the scene; in golf a bunker is a sand-filled hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers in the USA call a bunker a sand trap, so the shorter word is a synonym for that hazard.
